Pool surrounds, ramps, steps and slopes

Sealed and grippy, rather than sealed and slippery

A standard topical sealer puts a smooth film on a surface, which protects it and can make it slippery when wet. An anti slip system is the same sealer with a fine aggregate suspended in the coat, so the surface keeps a texture underfoot. On a pool surround, a ramp or a set of steps that is the difference that matters.

  • Fine aggregate in the coat, not on top of it
  • Protection and grip from one system
  • Small cost increase over a standard seal

Why it exists

Topical sealers are films. A film is smoother than the concrete under it, and a smooth wet film is slippery. On a driveway that is irrelevant. On a pool surround walked on by wet children, on steps, on a ramp or on a sloped crossover it is the single most important property the surface has.

The fix is an aggregate additive mixed into the sealer so it is suspended through the coat rather than broadcast onto the top of it. Suspended, it wears at the same rate as the sealer and the grip lasts as long as the coating. Broadcast on top, it wears off the high points within a year and you are back to a smooth film.

Where it matters

Ranked by how badly it matters

Surfaces where grip is worth more than appearance, in the order we would argue for it.
  Why Our view
Pool surrounds Permanently wet, walked on barefoot, often by children We would not seal one any other way
Steps and stair treads The highest consequence slip surface anywhere on a property Always, including internal to external transitions
Ramps and sloped access Gravity plus water. Wheelchair and trolley access especially Always, and often a compliance requirement
Sloped driveways and crossovers People walk down them in the rain carrying things Strongly recommended on anything steep
Alfresco and outdoor dining Wet underfoot, people in socks and bare feet Worth it, particularly with a gloss finish
Commercial entries and walkways Public liability, and wet floors from rain at the door Yes, and often specified
Flat open driveways Vehicles, and nobody walks on them wet Usually unnecessary. We will say so

Honest limits

Three things it is not

Not a slip rating certificate

Formal slip resistance testing is a specialist service with its own standards and instruments. Where a commercial project needs a certified rating, that needs a testing authority and we will tell you that rather than implying our product provides it.

Not invisible

The additive gives the surface a very fine texture, which is slightly visible in raking light and definitely noticeable underfoot. That is the point, and most people cannot see it at all from standing height.

Not a fix for a smooth polished surface

If the underlying surface is polished stone or glazed tile, a sealer with grit in it helps but it is working against the material. Sometimes the right answer is a different surface, not a different coating.

Questions

Asked about grip

Does anti slip sealing change how the surface looks?

Slightly. The additive gives a very fine texture that is visible in raking light and obvious underfoot, and almost invisible from standing height. Colour and sheen are otherwise the same as a standard sealer in that finish.

We can do a test area so you can see and feel it before committing the whole surface.

How much more does it cost than a normal seal?

A small increase, because it is the same sealer with an additive in it rather than a different product or a different process. It is one of the cheapest safety decisions available on a property.

Will it wear off?

Not independently of the sealer, because the aggregate is suspended through the coat rather than sprinkled on top. It wears at the same rate as the coating, so the grip lasts as long as the seal does.

An additive broadcast onto the surface of a wet coat does wear off the high points within a year, which is worth knowing when comparing quotes.

Is it harder to clean?

Marginally. A textured surface holds a little more than a smooth one, so it wants sweeping rather than just hosing. Against that, it is sealed, so nothing is going into it.

On balance an anti slip sealed surface is easier to keep clean than an unsealed textured one by a wide margin.

Can you add it to a surface that is already sealed?

Only as part of a recoat, because the aggregate has to be in the coat. Broadcasting grit onto an existing sealer gives you grip for a season and a mess afterwards.

If the existing sealer is near the end of its life anyway, that is the right time to do it.

Is it suitable for a commercial entry?

Yes, and it is commonly specified. What we cannot provide is a certified slip resistance rating, which needs a testing authority with the right instruments.

If your project requires a documented rating, arrange testing and we will work to the specification that comes out of it.
